output.summary: A deciduous tree native to eastern and central North America, red mulberry has rough, sandpaper-like upper leaf surfaces and soft-haired undersides. Its blackberry-like fruit ripens from pale green to red or dark purple. The sweet berries are eaten raw, used in pastries or preserves, and fermented into wine; Powhatan people also ate them, sometimes boiled.
